ablations.prompt: Can you break down inflation for a kid? under 60 words, and simple enough for a grade 5 reader to follow.

runs.answer: Inflation means prices go up over time. Imagine a candy bar that cost 50 cents last year and costs 60 cents now. Your money buys a little less candy than it used to. That's inflation!

Inflation means prices go up over time. Last year, a candy bar cost one dollar. This year, the same candy bar costs one dollar and twenty cents. That means your dollar can buy less candy than it could before. When prices keep rising like this, we call it inflation.

ablations.prompt: Can you break down inflation for a kid? Three bullet points exactly, and simple enough for a grade 5 reader to follow.

runs.answer:
- Inflation means prices go up over time. Something that cost $1 when your grandparents were kids might cost $5 today.

- It happens when there is more money around to buy things, or when things get harder to make, so stores can charge more and people are still willing to pay.

- Because of inflation, your money buys a little less each year, so saving it under your mattress means it can slowly lose its buying power.

- Inflation means prices go up over time. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were kids might cost a dollar or more today.

- Money slowly buys less. If prices rise and your allowance stays the same, you can afford fewer things with it than you could before.

- Usually, inflation happens a little bit each year. Lots of things, like food, toys, and gas, cost more as time goes on, and people's pay often goes up too to keep up.
